target_customer: Production and custom homebuilders that pay for buyer-facing apps and operations software
problem: New home buyers deal with fragmented communication, documents and warranty requests across a long build, and builders lack modern software for that experience.

founders.name: Luke Groesbeck
founders.background_notes: 15+ years starting and scaling venture-backed startups as founder, PM and product executive (YC page).

technical_complexity.rationale: White-label buyer apps and portals are standard web and mobile engineering, with integrations into builder systems being the harder part.

defensibility.rationale: Builder relationships from the founders' Opendoor channel and embedded customer apps create stickiness, but the product category is copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. CB Insights lists Higharc as a competitor, though its dating relative to 2023 is not established.

market_need_then: The founders sold into homebuilders at Opendoor and saw the buyer journey remained offline; no independent dated demand evidence was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses buildwithfoundation.com, a prefixed domain, indicating the exact name domain was not used.
branding.community_and_virality: Founder podcast appearance on a new home sales podcast; no merch or community evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear one-liner but the name is very generic and conflicts with many other Foundation companies, including Foundation custom homes software.

outcome_analysis: Foundation, built by ex-Opendoor homebuilder channel leaders, sells white-label buyer apps and warranty tools to builders. Secondary profiles claim fivefold growth in 2025 and more than 10,000 homes a year sold through the platform, but these are company-reported and no verified funding round or exit was found, so the outcome is early and unproven.
notes: The company website buildwithfoundation.com could not be fetched because the fetch tool's domain safety check was rate-limited. Funding figures conflict across aggregators (130K, 500K convertible note, 6.8M, 11M) and no press release or second outlet was found, so no round is recorded. Another database lists Graham Place as a third co-founder; YC page does not list him as a founder so he is omitted. Competitors found were undated CB Insights listings, so the list is empty. Completeness pass: CB Insights lists a $500K convertible note (no date given); this round rests on a single database. Extruct ($11M), Simplify ($130K and $6.8M) conflict and are not recorded or summed. No press release or filing found.
